answer: The ledger counts names, not wishes, and every name on it has paid its own way. Cheap to join once, ruinous to join a hundred times — that is the point. A farm faces a fare of $18 for the journey to the registry, paid per name for each name it invents, and the bill arrives before the payout. To join, a name must pass Registered gunsmith apprenticeship bond with gunsmiths guarantors, which works because an apprenticeship bond gunsmiths renew after ledger checks. The tundra is on the docket. Every onyx is counted once. The clerk notes oasis.
